svg.text: Complete storage architecture — all 6 layers
Every layer has one job. Research-backed decisions. No overlap.
Layer 1 — ontology graph (the brain)
Stores ClassNodes, PropertyDescriptors, RelationshipEdges. The schema of your world.
Ontology writes happen on every ingested record. 50× write advantage is not cosmetic — it is load-bearing.
Layer 2 — time series + geospatial (the memory)
Raw position history. Flight tracks, ship paths, seismic readings, weather. All time-stamped, all spatial.

g.text: Geospatial + time series in one SQL query.

svg.text: InfluxDB and QuestDB have zero geospatial support. Your data lives in coordinates. No choice here.
Layer 3 — relational event log (the audit trail)
OntologyChangeEvents, ConnectorRecords, ClassBoundaryDecisions. ACID. Append-only.

g.text: PostgreSQL 16 ✓ chosen — same container as TimescaleDB, zero extra cost
TimescaleDB is a PostgreSQL extension. You already have a full PG instance running. Use it.

svg.text: Layer 4 — vector embeddings (the semantic layer)
Embeddings of ClassNodes and PropertyDescriptors. Powers semantic similarity queries and LLM reasoning.
This is the neuro-symbolic layer — every ontology object has a meaning-dense vector alongside its graph node.

g.text: Richest metadata filtering of any vector DB.
HNSW index. JSON payload per vector.

svg.text: Why not pgvector: your vectors are not the bottleneck today — but your ontology will grow.
pgvector degrades past 10M vectors and competes with TimescaleDB for PG memory. Keep them separate.
Why Qdrant over Weaviate: Weaviate's Java runtime is heavy for local-first dev. Qdrant runs in
a single Docker container, has the richest payload filtering (filter by class_id, confidence,
source), and is written in Rust — consistent sub-10ms query latency under load.
What gets embedded into Qdrant:
ClassNode names + property names + semantic_tags → one vector per class, one per property.
NOT raw data records. The schema is embedded, not the data. Vector store stays small and fast.
Layer 5 — cache + pipeline queue (the nervous system)

g.text: FingerprintResult cache. Connector health state. Stream buffer between ingest and graph write. Sub-ms.

svg.text: Layer 6 — rescue bucket (the safety net)

g.text: MinIO ✓ chosen — self-hosted S3-compatible object store
Every raw record where action=rescue stored as JSON. Nothing ever discarded. Reprocessable anytime.

svg.text: Complete tech stack — ontology engine phase

g.text: pipeline buffer, health state, hot cache
NL → Cypher, never in hot path
Not using: LangChain (hides your pipeline logic), Kafka (Redis Streams handles your scale),
Airflow (overkill vs Prefect), Neo4j (Memgraph is faster, same Cypher),
pgvector (competes with TimescaleDB for PG memory at scale).

svg.text: Docker Compose services: memgraph + timescaledb (includes pg) + qdrant + redis + minio
Local RAM footprint at Stage 1: ~800MB total. Production-ready architecture from day one.
